1.pericope_label: Sing, O barren, and enlarge thy tent
debates: Who the barren woman represents
Whether the promise is of a restored nation or of the church at large
What the prohibition against sparing implies
outliers: Clarke refers the chapter to a future conversion of the Jews where Wesley and Henry read it of the church of Christ
themes: A song following a chapter of suffering
A tent chosen for a movable and mean condition
Weak faith declining the room offered it
Extent promised beyond what was ever possessed

debates: What the shame of youth and the reproach of widowhood refer to
What the plural forms Makers and Husbands imply
What the title Redeemer contributes
outliers: Keil and Delitzsch read the plurals as revelation absorbing what is true in polytheism, where Gill reads them of the three persons
themes: Shame forgotten rather than merely removed
A widowhood only apparent
Kinship as the ground of rescue
A title widened from one nation to the earth

6.pericope_label: A wife recalled, and wrath that lasts a moment
debates: Whether the forsaking is real or only apparent
Whether the wrath described is little or overflowing
What period the small moment covers
outliers: Gill and Keil and Delitzsch both report that the word rendered little wrath may mean its opposite
themes: Consolation drawn from a marriage figure
Affliction counted and remembered by God
A comparison that measures wrath against desert
Wrath timed against kindness without end

9.pericope_label: The waters of Noah, and a covenant of peace that cannot be shaken
debates: Whether the text reads as the waters or as the days of Noah
Whether the departing mountains are literal, comparative or figurative
Whether the oath sworn to Noah was strictly an oath or a covenant
outliers: Clarke prefers the reading as the waters where the ancient versions he lists mostly render days
themes: An oath as the ground of security
A promise measured against the most durable things in the world
Affliction as the furnace a glorified church passes through
Peace as a word that reaches as far as salvation

11.pericope_label: Stones laid with fair colours, and gates of carbuncle
debates: Whether the gems carry particular symbolic meanings or are general images of splendour
Which stone the word rendered agates denotes
Whether windows or pinnacles is the right rendering
outliers: Clarke denies the precise symbolism that Ellicott builds on the parallel of the high priestly breastplate
themes: God noticing the church when no one else comforts her
Splendour promised to what now lies in rubble
Treasure of this world used as pavement
Light let in as the image of teaching

13.pericope_label: All thy children taught of the LORD
debates: Whether taught of the Lord means taught directly or through appointed means
Whether the righteousness that establishes is imputed or practised
Whether the peace promised is inward, outward or both
outliers: Ellicott reads the clause as a title, disciples of Jehovah, where the others read it as a promise of instruction
themes: A promise that excludes none of the children
Teaching that begins with self-knowledge
Character and glory strengthening one another
Freedom from fear grounded in what has been given rather than in circumstances

15.pericope_label: No weapon formed against thee shall prosper
debates: Whether the gatherers fall before the city or come over to its side
Who the smith and the waster represent
Whether the passage speaks of the historical Jerusalem or of the church
outliers: Clarke renders the clause shall come over to thy side against the received sense that the gatherer shall fall
themes: Attack permitted but not commissioned
The maker of the weapon as the guarantee against it
Deliverance extended from war to accusation
A heritage received rather than achieved
